newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif, toll revenues rise - official.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif, toll revenues rise - official.

text.p: Toll revenues from Orange County's Foothill Transportation Corridor toll road surpassed projections for the first time in October, tollway officials said on Monday.
Revenues for the month were $600,909, just over the $594,800 projected and an 8 percent increase over the previous month's record high.
During the month, toll transactions on the Foothill Transportation Corridor totalled 1,082,684 transactions, up 9 percent from the previous month, officials said.

In September, toll revenues matched projections for the 7.5-mile corridor, according to Walter Kreutzen, executive vice president of finance and administration for the Transportation Corridor Agencies, which oversees the project.
"We've clearly demonstrated that Californians will use toll roads," Kreutzen said.
"Have we turned the corner?" he added. "I think we have turned the corner in that the roads are performing at expectations."
Toll revenues from the Foothill Transportation Corridor for the fiscal year that ended June 30 were below projections.
To fund tollway construction, about $1.5 billion of bonds were sold based in part on expectations of tollway revenues.
